thesis: Useful clinical AI should earn adoption through its work while preserving a patient's ability to refuse without losing care.
editorial_arc: TCC's announced narrow clerical workflow and provider authority
Separate recordings, chart notes and possible reuse
Fair affirmative case and measured-benefit limit
Attributed refusal promise and care-first standard

source_mapping.passage: Less typing and more patient attention are an aim
Provider review, edits, approval and clinical judgment
Possible reuse of deidentified portions and unresolved retention question
No measured benefits reported in the notice
Decline or change one's mind without affecting care, explicitly attributed

scope_controls: Benefits described as aims or possibilities, not measured outcomes
Recording deletion not extended to chart notes or reused portions
No claim of privacy failure or separate reuse opt-out
Refusal terms are TCC's promise, not audited patient experience
No private patient details, political claims, URLs, source list, credits or social posting
hashtag_rationale: ArtificialIntelligence is the broad topic, Alaska is the geographic topic, TribalHealth and PatientConsent are the narrow subject areas. No live audience-size or reach claims are made.

independent_review.required_next: Separate editor and scorer must review against config/linkedin_caption_rubric.yaml. This writer has not claimed an independent score.
